title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics
book_title: Chapter 3: How It Is Sold & Delivered — Distribution & Unit Economics
question: How does SK hynix qualify, price, and deliver memory across Korea, China, and the U.S., and how does $100 of FY2025 revenue flow down to free cash flow?

epigraph.quote: In the case of HBM, we need much more time to adjust chips inside our customers' systems to maximize performance.
epigraph.author: Kwak Noh-jung, CEO of SK hynix Inc., August 2026

web_blocks.title: Go-to-market model: Direct OEM qualification, LTAs, and foundry co-packaging

web_blocks.html: SK hynix sells almost entirely through direct B2B engineering teams rather than retail channels. For HBM3E and HBM4, the sales cycle runs an 18-month technical loop. Engineers co-design base-die interfaces, signal integrity, and heat profiles with GPU and ASIC teams like NVIDIA and AMD [2, 13]. They then qualify the physical stack through foundry partners such as TSMC [2, 13]. Once qualified, Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) govern volume and price bands. By Q3 2026, LTAs with 14 key clients already covered over 50% of 2027–2028 capacity [2, 13].

For server DDR5, mobile LPDDR5, and Solidigm eSSDs, SK hynix sells directly to hyperscalers (AWS, Microsoft, Google, Meta) and OEMs. Pricing resets through quarterly contract talks, with a small channel network for client PC SSDs. Because HBM stacks are custom-fit to specific accelerator boards, mid-generation switching costs are high. That gives SK hynix far better pricing visibility than traditional spot DRAM.

web_blocks.title: Global manufacturing footprint: Korea core, China legacy exposure, and U.S. expansion

web_blocks.html: Core production sits in South Korea at Icheon (M14, M16 EUV DRAM) and Cheongju (M15, M15X DRAM/HBM, and NAND) [18]. To serve 2027–2030 demand, SK hynix sped up tool move-ins at M15X and is building the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster [18, 19]. Yongin targets early 2027 cleanroom readiness [19]. In August 2026, SK hynix also broke ground on a $3.87B–$4B packaging hub in West Lafayette, Indiana [8, 10]. Backed by up to $458M in CHIPS Act grants and $500M in loans, Indiana will package Korean wafers domestically by 2028–2029 [8, 10].

The main geographic risk sits in China. SK hynix runs a large legacy DRAM fab in Wuxi and acquired Intel's Dalian NAND fab via Solidigm [16]. U.S. export rules restrict advanced American chipmaking tools from entering China [14, 16]. That complicates upgrades at Wuxi and Dalian. In response, SK hynix is shifting leading-edge nodes back to Korea and HBM packaging to Indiana [14, 16].

Audited FY2025 results (ended December 31, 2025) show how a fab-heavy model converts sales into cash [1, 17]. At ~1,426 KRW/USD, FY2025 revenue of $68.13B (KRW 97.15T) produced $42.88B in EBITDA (62.9% margin) [1]. Operating profit reached $33.11B (48.6% margin) after $9.77B in non-cash depreciation [1]. Heavy capex of $20.06B (KRW 28.60T) absorbed just over half of $37.36B in operating cash flow [1]. That still left $17.30B in free cash flow, or $25.39 per $100 of sales.

web_blocks.caption: Audited FY2025 $100 Revenue-to-Free-Cash-Flow Waterfall (converted from KRW 97.15T audited consolidated results)
web_blocks.takeaway: Out of every $100 of FY2025 sales, SK hynix kept $62.94 in EBITDA, absorbed $14.34 in depreciation and $7.74 in taxes, generated $54.84 in operating cash flow, reinvested $29.44 into fab capex, and banked $25.39 in free cash flow.

web_blocks.html: The waterfall shows the core trade-off of owning memory fabs. Even in a boom year with 48.6% operating margins, nearly 30% of every sales dollar went straight into cleanrooms and EUV tools ($20.06B capex). In a downturn, revenue can drop 30% to 40% while $9.77B in depreciation and fab shell costs stay fixed. When that happens, the $25.39 free cash flow cushion can turn negative fast unless management cuts equipment orders early.

web_blocks.takeaway: SK hynix's leading-edge HBM engine sits inside South Korea and is expanding into Indiana packaging, while its legacy China fabs face ongoing U.S. equipment-upgrade restrictions.

web_blocks.html: This geographic split drove capital spending to ~KRW 28.60T ($20.06B) in FY2025 and kept it high in 2026 [19]. Because U.S. export rules block advanced tool upgrades at Wuxi and Dalian, China fabs cannot supply next-generation bits [16]. Instead, SK hynix must fund new cleanrooms in Cheongju (M15X), Yongin, and Indiana at the same time [8, 18, 19]. Those builds lock in high fixed depreciation charges for the next decade.

book_paragraphs: Memory chips are not sold off a shelf. When you and I look at how SK hynix gets its silicon into an AI server, the process looks much more like aerospace contracting than consumer electronics.

For HBM3E and HBM4, SK hynix engineers work inside the customer's design loop eighteen months before a chip ships. They tune electrical timing, power delivery, and heat dissipation to match a specific AI processor, then qualify the stacked module through TSMC's packaging line. Once a customer designs a board around SK hynix's stack, they sign multi-quarter Long-Term Agreements. By late 2026, fourteen major customers had already locked up over half of SK hynix's capacity for 2027 and 2028.

Manufacturing that silicon spans three countries with very different geopolitical profiles. The crown-jewel DRAM and HBM fabs sit in Icheon and Cheongju in South Korea, soon to be joined by the massive Yongin cluster. In August 2026, SK hynix broke ground on a nearly $4 billion advanced packaging plant in West Lafayette, Indiana, so Korean wafers can be stacked and tested on U.S. soil by 2028–2029. Meanwhile, older DRAM and NAND fabs in Wuxi and Dalian, China face ongoing U.S. equipment export hurdles.

Understanding how SK hynix ships its chips also means understanding its geographic tightrope. Front-end wafer fabrication is heavily concentrated in South Korea at Icheon and Cheongju, where extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines pattern features just a few nanometers wide.

At the same time, SK hynix still operates two large legacy plants in China: a DRAM fab in Wuxi and the Dalian NAND fab it acquired from Intel through Solidigm. U.S. Commerce Department export rules have made it difficult to ship advanced American chipmaking tools into China for upgrades, creating a Catch-22 for Solidigm's cash flow and U.S. expansion plans.

That is why SK hynix broke ground in West Lafayette, Indiana in August 2026 with a nearly $4 billion commitment backed by CHIPS Act incentives. By shipping Korean DRAM wafers to Indiana for 2.5D and 3D HBM stacking by 2028–2029, SK hynix puts final HBM assembly right next to its biggest American hyperscale customers.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Capex Tax on Every Dollar of Sales
book_callouts.text: Look closely at the FY2025 waterfall. Out of every $100 in sales, SK hynix generated $54.84 in operating cash flow—and immediately spent $29.44 of it on new fabs and EUV tools. That leaves $25.39 in true free cash flow. In software, margins are free; in memory, you have to buy next year's factory out of this year's profits.

book_subsections.title: Walking Through $100 of FY2025 Revenue
paragraphs: Start with $100 of revenue in FY2025. Direct manufacturing costs excluding depreciation took $25.25, R&D engineering compensation took $6.93, and other SG&A overhead took $4.89. That left $62.94 in operating EBITDA—an extraordinary cash margin for hardware.

Subtract $14.34 for depreciation on prior fab investments, adjust for modest interest and non-operating treasury income, and pay $7.74 in corporate taxes, and accounting net profit landed at $44.22 per $100 of sales. Adding back non-cash depreciation and working-capital inflows lifted operating cash flow to $54.84. After $29.44 in capital expenditures, owners kept $25.39 in free cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Why Working Capital and Capex Discipline Decide the Downcycle
paragraphs: In a boom year like FY2025, working capital works in SK hynix's favor. Customers prepay or settle invoices promptly to secure scarce HBM allocations, pushing operating cash flow to $37.36 billion—well above accounting net income.

In a downturn, that script flips. Inventory days stretch as PC and smartphone buyers delay orders, while multi-year cleanroom shells at Yongin and Indiana cannot be paused halfway through construction without wasting billions. Keeping free cash flow positive across a full cycle depends on throttling wafer-equipment orders early whenever LTA demand cools.
